title: Divine Redemption
english: God exists, and He is the provider of existence and the cause of being for those who do not exist. He says to sinners, 'I will still help,' giving confidence that despite many and insurmountable causes, a remnant of gentleness and philanthropy is preserved, and if they choose to follow what is better and more suitable, He will not refuse to save them.

He will give water to those who thirst and walk in a waterless land, and He will put His Spirit upon their seed and His blessings upon their children. They will spring up like grass in the midst of water and like willows by flowing water, and one will say, 'I am of God,' and another will call upon the name of Jacob, and another will write, 'I am of God,' on the name of Israel.

It seems that in these passages, Israel and Jacob refer to the chorus of holy apostles as one entity, for all are one in Christ. Since they are from the blood of Jacob and Israel, they have become precious and chosen vessels, called to the priesthood of the evangelical proclamation.

God says that He loves and has not rejected them, although it is clear that He would not have called those who have faith in Him beloved and chosen. He will crown them with such bright voices, as they will shine like stars in the world, holding the word of life and guiding those under the sun.

Do not fear, for this means being courageous and strong, and having a steadfast and youthful mindset, laughing at the attacks of persecutors, and having unwavering faith in God. For most of those who fight against sacred teachings will be opposed by a multitude of wicked people.

But you will be better than cowardice and laziness, for I will give water to those walking in a waterless land, which is a pleasant and salvific thing for those walking in thirst. It is even more desirable to be nourished by divine and spiritual things, that is, by spiritual consolations, through which the human mind, having become weak, may be somewhat strengthened towards courage. The water that God promises to provide to those walking in a waterless land is, we say, the Holy Spirit, as the Savior himself said, 'Rivers of living water will flow from his belly' (John 7:38).

title: Christ the Foundation
english: Christ bringing all to the knowledge of the truth, calling to repentance, justifying through faith, and making renowned through sanctification, the heavenly spirits rejoiced because God had mercy on Israel, not only the physical but also the spiritual.
The foundations of the earth, which are the ministers of the evangelical decrees, were established, and their sound went out everywhere.

Certain sacred trumpets sounded, proclaiming the glory of the Savior to all and calling to knowledge of Christ those from circumcision and those who formerly worshiped the creation instead of the Creator.

Christ is the foundation and unshakeable base of all, bearing all and holding together the things that were falling, and we are all being built upon him, a spiritual house, being fitted together through the Spirit into a holy temple, a dwelling place for him.

He dwells in our hearts through faith, and the apostles and evangelists, who were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word, became a foundation for the faith, and we must follow their traditions to keep the faith straight and uncorrupted.
For Christ said to Peter, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God,' and 'You are Peter, and on this rock I will found my Church' (Matthew 16:16, 18).

The foundations of it are in the holy mountains (Psalm 87:1), and the holy mountains are to be understood as the holy apostles and evangelists, whose knowledge to those who come after them is like a foundation, preventing them from being shaken toward what is worthless in faith.

In contrast to Moses, who was weak in speech and slow of tongue, those who preach Christ sound a clear message, and their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world (Psalm 19:4, Romans 10:18).
The foundations of the earth are sounding, and the illustrious disciples, known everywhere, are sounding the message of Christ.
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmentary at the beginning and end; the initial participial clause lacks a finite verb, and the final word 'γν' is cut off, so the translation renders the participial phrase literally with a trailing ellipsis and notes the incompleteness.

title: Christ as the embodiment of mercy and righteousness through human incarnation
english: Christ has become for us both umpire and teacher. One might say that mercy and righteousness, which rise from the earth or even sprout forth, is none other than our Lord Jesus Christ. For he has indeed become for us, from God the Father, both mercy and righteousness, if it is true that we have been shown mercy in him and have been justified—having received forgiveness for our ancient offenses, or rather, having received from him the power to attain the righteousness that brings every good to its completion, by which we are also saved.

But if the earth has been commanded to bring forth righteousness, let no one take offense, upon reflecting that even the Psalmist somewhere declares concerning God and Father, and even concerning Emmanuel himself: 'He has worked righteousness in the midst of the earth.' For Christ did not descend his flesh from above or from heaven; rather, he came into being according to the flesh from a woman, who also became one of those upon the earth. Therefore, whenever it is said that the earth produces fruit and vegetation, you will understand, as I have said, that he came according to the flesh from a woman taken up for this very ministry—though she is but one among those who belong to the earth.

'I am the Lord your God who created you.' What better thing have I fashioned than clay for the potter? They give this reason in such matters: that even God, being by nature the Son, emptied himself, took upon himself the form of a servant, and suffered for our sake—yes, for 352 of us—and deemed worthy of such great mercy those who dwell upon the earth, as if to offer his own soul in exchange. But more than that, he undertook to take the form of the servant and to transform the utter insignificance of human nature from the height of divine glory.

He says that I am now to be understood as having existed and living, not as having begun just now; for God is true, the Lord of all powers, who brought all things into being without making death, but rather creating everything for incorruption. Then, honoring human nature, he observes that among all earthly creatures nothing could ever fully equal it, asking what better thing he could have formed than a potter shapes clay; for we were formed by him taking dust from the earth and shaping it with great skill, as a potter molds his vessel. Yet the worth of human nature extends even beyond this, for within us lies something greater, foreign and a gift of God’s own skill. Indeed, we have been made according to his image and likeness, and we have inwardly enriched the character of his glory so that it shines upon our souls, even though we remain according to flesh, earthly and from the earth. Therefore, humanity on earth is not contemptible but rather worthy of amazement as a living creature, and thus God is exalted in him. Indeed, he said to the most enduring Job, making his mighty works evident: ‘Having taken clay from the earth, you formed a living creature and set it to speak upon the ground?’
Psalle.
